purpose: Deflazacort is used to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients who are 2 years of age and older. It helps slow down the muscle weakness and loss of muscle function that comes with this condition. It is not a cure, but it can help preserve muscle strength and improve quality of life.
how_it_works: Deflazacort is a type of steroid that works by calming down inflammation in the body. In Duchenne muscular dystrophy, inflammation contributes to muscle damage, so by reducing that inflammation, the medication helps protect the muscles. Think of it as turning down the volume on the body's overactive inflammatory response to help muscles last longer.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include weight gain, a puffy or rounded face (sometimes called 'moon face'), increased appetite, mood changes or irritability, trouble sleeping, slowed growth in children, and increased risk of infections. You may also notice increased hair growth or acne.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly — your doctor needs to slowly lower the dose to avoid serious problems. This medicine can weaken your immune system, making it harder to fight infections, so avoid contact with people who are sick. Tell your doctor if you have diabetes, high blood pressure, osteoporosis, or eye problems like cataracts or glaucoma, as this medicine can worsen those conditions. Also let your doctor know about all other medications you take, as many drugs can interact with deflazacort.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is about 0.9 mg per kilogram of body weight taken once daily by mouth. It comes as tablets or an oral suspension (liquid). Your doctor will calculate the right dose based on your child's weight and may adjust it over time. It is best taken with food to help reduce stomach upset.
